ordered_diagnoses: Primary cutaneous anaplastic large cell lymphoma

salient_findings: Confluent lichenified erythromelanotic plaques with overlying thick greasy scales
Superficial dermal band-like lymphocytic infiltrate with dermal fibrosis
key_facts: Previous treatment with oral prednisolone and cyclosporine without improvement
Skin punch biopsies showed epidermotropism of atypical lymphocytes
Immunohistochemical staining showed tumor cells positive for CD3 and CD45RO
CD30 was positive in fewer than 25% of lymphocytes

differentials: Primary cutaneous anaplastic large cell lymphoma
per_call: Primary cutaneous anaplastic large cell lymphoma

shortlist: Primary cutaneous anaplastic large cell lymphoma

shortlist.label: Mycosis fungoides
shortlist.why_kept: Epidermotropism of atypical lymphocytes and dermal fibrosis are characteristic features

shortlist.label: Sézary syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of erythroderma and lymphadenopathy sparing, with atypical lymphocytes in skin biopsies

shortlist.label: Cutaneous T-cell lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Immunohistochemical staining showed tumor cells positive for CD3 and CD45RO, consistent with T-cell origin

shortlist.label: Folliculotropic mycosis fungoides
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation of progressive erythroderma with lymphocytic infiltration and absence of palpable lymphadenopathy

shortlist.label: Primary cutaneous anaplastic large cell lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: CD30 positivity in fewer than 25% of lymphocytes, although less typical, still a consideration given the overall clinical picture

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of erythroderma, epidermotropism of atypical lymphocytes, and immunohistochemical staining positive for CD3 and CD45RO are consistent with mycosis fungoides. The absence of palpable lymphadenopathy and the specific immunophenotypic profile also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Sézary syndrome
rejected.why: Sézary syndrome typically presents with more systemic involvement and lymphadenopathy, which is not present in this case.

rejected.label: Cutaneous T-cell lymphoma
rejected.why: This is a broader category that includes mycosis fungoides, but the specific findings in this case are more consistent with mycosis fungoides.

rejected.label: Folliculotropic mycosis fungoides
rejected.why: The presence of follicular involvement is not mentioned, making this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Primary cutaneous anaplastic large cell lymphoma
rejected.why: The immunohistochemical staining profile, particularly the lack of widespread CD30 positivity, does not support this diagnosis.
